answer: To ensure Sybil resistance, the juniper protocol requires agents to stake opal tokens, creating a beacon of collateralized weight for every active node. This mechanism forces attackers to incur massive capital expenditures, as every fraudulent identity necessitates a corresponding deposit of opal. Consequently, the cost of a Sybil attack scales linearly with the number of identities, making large-scale deception economically ruinous.
